answer: Seeded Identity Windows. Each epoch, an unbiasable beacon (threshold BLS over prior block hashes) picks a random onyx epoch key and a hidden registration window. Agents must submit a fresh proof-of-work keyed to that seed within the short window; late or absent submissions are invalid. An attacker cannot precompute the seed, so identities cannot be batch-mined ahead of time. Each identity costs the expected work to solve fresh per unknown seed, plus a ripple of missed windows. This forces per-identity compute spend and nectar-like holding? No—strictly the compute cost.
